therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: B-cell depletion via antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: B-cell mediated immune suppression to reduce neuroinflammation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Annualized Relapse Rate (ARR) up to 96 weeks

results.target_engagement_evidence: Gd-enhancing T1 lesion rate ratio 0.033 (95% CI: 0.019–0.058), p<0.0001, indicating near-complete suppression of active inflammatory lesions
biomarker_changes: Gd-enhancing T1 lesions: 0.016 (ublituximab) vs 0.491 (teriflunomide) per scan per participant
New/enlarging T2 lesions: 0.213 (ublituximab) vs 2.789 (teriflunomide) per scan per participant
Brain volume percent change: -0.197% (ublituximab) vs -0.125% (teriflunomide), LS mean difference -0.072%, p<0.0001
subgroup_findings: NEDA (Week 24–96): 44.6% ublituximab vs 15.0% teriflunomide, OR 5.442 (95% CI: 3.536–8.375), p<0.0001
Impaired SDMT: 29.2% ublituximab vs 31.8% teriflunomide, OR 0.872 (95% CI: 0.603–1.261), p=0.4669 (not significant)
12-week CDP: median not reached in either arm due to low event numbers
safety_signals: Anaphylactic reaction and hypersensitivity SAEs observed in ublituximab arm (infusion-related reactions)
Pneumonia SAEs higher in ublituximab arm (3/273 vs 0/275)
Central nervous system enteroviral infection: 2/273 ublituximab vs 0/275 teriflunomide

context.duration: Up to 96 weeks treatment; up to approximately 116 weeks total
